Unitary modular forms for U(2) — pieces matched to LMFDB newforms

Fields done so far: all with hK ≤ 3, and hK = 4 up to dK = −312 (plus −323, I2, weight [0,0]) (computations skipped by the time limits are not listed). Lattices I2 and diag(1,2), weights [0,0], [2,0], [3,1]; classical weight k = a − b + 2. Each Hecke-irreducible piece is matched with PARI against every newform of weight k and level dividing 4|dK|, at all good primes 3 ≤ p < 30: inert λ = ap2/pk−2 − (p+1); split (weight 0) λ2n = ap2n, n = exponent of Cl(K); split (higher weight, 1-dim pieces) N(λ) = ap2/pk−2. These rules do not see twists by genus characters, so twist-equivalent forms are listed together, smallest level first. Labels follow LMFDB ordering (orbits sorted by trace form). Bianchi links open the LMFDB Bianchi forms over K at the level norm predicted for the base change of the matched weight-2 newform (fields with |dK| < 700 only).

How to read this page (k, "up to a twist", Bianchi links, polynomials)

Why [2,0] and [3,1] both have k = 4

The weight [a,b] is the representation Syma−b(std) ⊗ detb. The classical weight only sees the symmetric power: k = a − b + 2. For [2,0] and [3,1] we have a − b = 2, so both correspond to weight-4 newforms. The extra det in [3,1] = [2,0] ⊗ det does not change k; it multiplies the Hecke eigenvalues at split primes by a value of a Hecke character of K (the factor in K that appears in the eigenvalues), and it changes which vectors are invariant under the automorphism groups, so the two spaces have different dimensions and different pieces, matched to the same or to different weight-4 newforms.

What "up to a twist" means

Twisting a newform f by a Dirichlet character χ gives f⊗χ with ap(f⊗χ) = χ(p)ap(f). On the unitary side, twisting by a genus character ψ of K multiplies the eigenvalue at a split prime P by ψ(P), and at split p the genus characters are exactly quadratic characters χd(p) with d | dK. The matching therefore uses quantities that do not see these signs: λ2n (weight [0,0]), N(λ) (higher weight) and the inert eigenvalues, which only involve ap2. So a piece determines its newform only up to f ↔ f⊗χd: all such twist-equivalent newforms that match are listed, smallest level first. Where Magma's own comparison (or a sign check at split primes) pinned down the twist, it is given in the "twist" column; otherwise "up to a twist" is written.

How the Bianchi links were made

The Bianchi link is not an individual match: it opens the LMFDB list of Bianchi newforms over K (field 2.0.|dK|.1), shown for weight-[0,0] pieces matched to a weight-2 newform. Base change predicts there the form F = BC(f) with aP(F) = ap(f) at split P (so λP = ±aP(F), the sign being the genus character) and a(p)(F) = ap(f)2 − 2p at inert p (so a(p)(F) = λ − p + 1). Click a row to see, prime by prime, the unitary polynomial and the polynomial these Bianchi eigenvalues must satisfy, to compare with the LMFDB Bianchi pages.

Atkin–Lehner signs and the "Expected vs found" tab

For each LMFDB label, wp = ±1 is its Atkin–Lehner eigenvalue at each prime p dividing its level (computed with PARI, same newforms and labels as the LMFDB); for twist pairs the signs are given for each member. The third tab lists, for every computed space, all newforms of level dividing |dK| (I2) or 2|dK| (diag(1,2)), says whether the following empirical rule expects them, and whether they occur. Let B be the quaternion algebra (dK, −det L) over Q, s = ∏ wp over the odd p | dK, and W = −1, +1, −1 for weights [0,0], [2,0], [3,1]. (1) Every odd prime where B ramifies must divide the level. (2) If every odd p | dK divides the level, the sign must be right: s = W for I2 (odd dK), s = W (2 split) or s = −W (2 inert) for diag(1,2); otherwise any signs occur. (3) For even dK, a 2-adic condition depending on v2(level) and dK/4 mod 8 or dK/8 mod 4 (see the "reason" column). Rows in orange do not fit.

The polynomial panel

Click any piece. For every prime p it shows the characteristic polynomial of Tp on that piece (its roots are the eigenvalues of the forms in the piece; a power such as (…)3 means the forms occur 3 times), and for weight [0,0] at inert p the predicted Bianchi polynomial P(x + p − 1). "s" = split, "i" = inert. Very long polynomials are shortened; the full ones are in the results file.
